# dsh-sidebar-session-provider-icon
English · 简体中文
*Synthetic English sidebar illustration, light theme on the left and dark theme on the right with th
e same rows: single vendor marks for Claude, GPT, Grok and Gemini, an aggregator route mark for Open
Code with the GLM vendor corner, and the composite badge for Magpie behind a gateway — Trae in the b
ottom-left transit corner, DeepSeek in the bottom-right vendor corner. `currentColor` marks follow t
he theme while Gemini, GLM and DeepSeek keep their brand color in both. It renders an isolated DSH i
nstance that has no model credentials, so badges and rows come from the plugin's own output rather t
han a recorded live session.*
In the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) sidebar every session row looks alike, so you cannot tell which provid
er and model a conversation uses without opening it. This plugin shows a provider + model icon in fr
ont of each session title, read from the model currently selected in the composer, and updates it th
e moment you switch. When the provider and the model come from different vendors (for example `openc
ode-go/deepseek-v4-flash`), the provider logo carries a small model logo in its bottom-right corner.
- **Real brand marks, nothing generated.** Logos are pinned, vendored SVGs chosen from the actual pr

ovider route and model id; nothing is generated or fetched at runtime.
- **Follows the composer live
.** The open session tracks the input-box selection immediately; other rows keep their next selectio

n, and cold history falls back to the last real request.
- **Gateway-aware composite.** Aggregator r
outes show the route logo with the model vendor in the corner, and gateways such as Magpie can add t
he transit platform as a third layer — all inside the original 14×14 footprint.
## Install
DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2`, Node.js `>=22.19`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart DSH and refresh the Web page. Nothing else is needed: no configuration, no network access, a
nd no files written outside the DSH profile that installs it.
## How it behaves
The logo shown for a session comes from three sources, in this order:
1. **Live selection (preferred, while verifiable).** The official `dsh-client-ui-model-selection` st
ore, read as `ctx.modelDirectories.directoryFor(sessionId).store.current`. It is the single per-sess
ion state shared by the input-box selector and the `/model` command, and it publishes `{ provider, m
odel }` as soon as `session.selectModel` succeeds. The open session, including a blank one that has
not sent a message yet, therefore follows the input-box selection. That store belongs to a client Se
ssion scope, so every session-list and DOM signal re-resolves it: when the runtime hands out a new s
tore for the same session (leaving the session and coming back is enough) the badge re-subscribes an
d re-reads it, and it re-reads the snapshot even when the identity did not change. An observation is
kept only while its session is the open one; once the view moves on — or the directory cannot be re

solved any more — it is dropped, so a value the client can no longer verify never decides a row.
2.
**Selected model (durable).** The official `modelSelection` projection's `next`: the selection the s
ession will use for its next request. The host maintains it and it also covers a model the user pick

ed but has not sent with yet, which is what keeps a row right after you leave its session.
3. **Last
request (cold-history fallback).** A Host `provider` session projection folds the `request/header`
events of the session log, so a history session whose selector has not been loaded in this browser s
till shows the provider of its most recent real request. It survives restarts and uses no `localStor
shows the provider of its most recent real request. It survives restarts and uses no `localStorage`.
Brand resolution has two independent dimensions: the provider route picks the **main logo**, the mod
el id picks the **corner logo**.

## Configuration
None. The plugin row carries no `config` fields and the package reads no environment variables.
## Provider / model → icon

rmines the main icon; a different known model brand determines the corner icon. `—` means that dimen
sion is not recognized for that brand. The exact rules live in `logos.ts`.
